knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Eggs are not moved without authority. Pausing the work and seeking guidance is the correct response.
Loose or sagging netting can entangle wildlife. It must be supported, secured and checked.
The lesson gives no wildlife authority. Relocating or handling native animals needs authority from the relevant agency.

practicalCriteria: Learner identifies a simulated nest or egg cluster and pauses the simulated work, recording the observation
Learner installs netting on a simulated pond, supported above the water and secured at the edges
Learner reports a simulated trapped animal without handling it
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Observation and pause record for nests or eggs
Assessor observation of the stop decision in a simulation
stopWorkCriteria: Nests, eggs or breeding animals present in the work area
Animal trapped in netting and the worker is not authorised to free it
Request to remove, relocate or harm wildlife
